Create an industrial harbor loading dock with shipping containers, barrels, cranes, warehouse props, pallets, and warning signs. Organize the dock around a recognizable cargo-handling area, with cranes as the principal vertical structures and groups of shipping containers forming the main storage masses. Arrange the containers in deliberate rows and compact groups so the dock reads as an organized industrial workplace. Leave clearer gaps between these groups to distinguish the loading area from the stored cargo. Place pallets and warehouse props near the containers and around the working area, using smaller clusters to suggest separate handling and storage points. Gather barrels beside some of the pallet groups and warehouse props rather than distributing them evenly across the entire dock. Put warning signs at the edges of working and storage areas where their relationship to the cargo-handling activity is visible. Keep the cranes, containers, and loading space visually dominant while using barrels, pallets, warehouse props, and signs to supply the smaller details. The overall arrangement should read clearly as a harbor loading dock with connected areas for handling and storing cargo.
